newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoros protesters demand governor's resignation.
newsitem.headline: Comoros protesters demand governor's resignation.

text.p: Protesters on the Indian Ocean Comoros island of Anjouan took to the streets to demand the resignation of the island governor and the withdrawal of security forces, witnesses said on Friday.
The protesters marched through the streets of Anjouan capital Mutsamudu on Thursday, chanting for the resignation of island governor Colonel Cheikh Allaui, who they consider a traitor.
They also demanded the withdrawal of security forces sent to Anjouan last month from the main Grande Comore island.
State radio said Comoro President Mohamed Taki would address the nation later on Friday on the Anjouan movement.

The Comoro Islands have a population of 190,000 and became independent from France in 1975. Residents of Anjouan, the second island, argue independence has brought only poverty, civil strife and numerous coups.
Three people including a gendarme were killed on Anjouan on July 14 in clashes involving secessionists who tried to raise French flags on Bastille Day. Several people were killed in March.
France has denounced the secessionists. It says the Anjouan situation was serious and could destabilise the whole region.
In another development, talks this week between secessionist leaders and Taki's government have led to tensions within the pro-secessionist movement.
"We have been betrayed once by the leaders who gave up after meeting Taki so we are highly cautious and we are not ready to be fooled again," one youth who declined to be named, told Reuters.

Secessionist leaders including Foundi Abdallah Ibrahim, 75, released from detention last week, have appealed for calm after the talks leading to a partial removal of some barricades blocking Mutsamudu streets, witnesses said.
Protesters on the Comoros' Moheli island demonstrated this week in favour of the Anjouan secessionists.
